title: Enums
intro: A Rust enum is a type with a fixed list of variants, and each variant can carry its own data. The compiler knows the full list, so it can check that you handled every variant.

coming_from.go: Go has no sum types. The closest is an interface plus a type switch (or `iota` constants, when there is no data). An interface is open: anyone can add a type, and Go does not check that a type switch covers them all. A Rust enum is a closed list of variants, and `match` won't compile until every variant is handled.
coming_from.kotlin: A Rust enum is your sealed class, and each variant is like a data subclass, with `match` checking every case the way `when` does. One difference: a variant is not its own type, so you can't have a parameter of type `Shape::Circle`.
coming_from.python: This is your union of dataclasses (`Circle | Rect`) plus `match`, in one declaration. The compiler checks that every variant is handled, and Python's `Enum` only covers variants that all hold the same kind of data, not different data per variant.
coming_from.typescript: A Rust enum is your discriminated union, but the compiler keeps the tag for you, so there is no `kind` field to write. `match` checks every variant without the `never` trick, and a `_` arm turns that check off the way `default:` does.
coming_from.java: A Rust `enum` with data is a `sealed interface` plus one `record` per variant, and `match` is the exhaustive pattern `switch`. Rust needs no separate types; the variants live inside the enum itself, as plain values rather than objects, and a variant is not a type of its own.
coming_from.csharp: A data-carrying `enum` is an `abstract record` with one derived record per case, and `match` is the positional pattern `switch`. On .NET 10 (C# 14) the compiler does not know that list is complete, so a missing case is a CS8509 warning and a run-time exception. In Rust it is a compile error. C# 15 adds `union` and `closed` types for this.
coming_from.c: A Rust `enum` is a tagged union (an `enum` tag plus a `union`) that the compiler manages for you. You can't read the wrong field for the current tag, and a `match` that forgets a variant doesn't compile.
coming_from.cpp: A Rust `enum` is a `std::variant`, except each alternative is a named variant, not a separate type, and `match` replaces `std::visit` with the `overloaded` helper. A missing case gets a short, clear error instead of a long template error.

notes: In a language without a closed list of cases, you fake it with an interface or base class plus type checks, and nothing makes sure you handled every case. In Rust, `match` checks that you did.
Rust's `match` pulls the data out of the variant: `Shape::Rect(w, h)` gives you `w` and `h`.
A variant is not a type of its own: `Shape::Circle` names a value, so a function can take a `Shape` but not a `Shape::Circle`.
An enum with no data works like a C enum: `Level::Mid as i32` gives its number.
Option and Result, in the next lessons, are ordinary enums like this one.

gotcha.title: Adding a variant and forgetting a case
gotcha.looks_fine: In Go you add `type Triangle struct{...}` and every type switch keeps compiling. A Triangle falls through to `return 0`, and the area is silently wrong.
gotcha.rust_sees: Rust knows the full list of variants, so it checks every `match` against it.
gotcha.why: This is the good kind of error. Add a variant, and the compiler gives you a to-do list of every place that needs updating.

go.says: Go runs this and prints 0, which is wrong. The compiler does not check that a type switch is complete, so `Triangle` falls through to `return 0` with no warning. A `default:` that panics would make it loud, if you remember to write one.

kotlin.says: Kotlin refuses this too: a `when` over a sealed class must cover every subclass, so adding `Triangle` breaks the build until you handle it. An `else ->` branch would silence the check.

python.says: Python prints None. No case matches the new Triangle, so `area` falls off the end and returns None instead of a number. Python itself gives no warning.

typescript.says: TypeScript refuses this too, because the `default` branch assigns the leftover value to `never` and a `triangle` is not `never` (TS2322). Without that `default` line, a function that returns a `number` still fails under `strict` (TS2366), but a function that returns nothing compiles, and the missing case goes unnoticed.

java.says: Java refuses this too: a switch expression over a sealed interface must cover every permitted type, so adding Triangle breaks the build until you handle it. The javac message does not name `Triangle`; Rust's E0004 does.

csharp.says: The compiler only warns that the switch is not exhaustive (CS8509). It cannot name `Triangle`, because a record hierarchy is not a closed list. The program builds, then throws a SwitchExpressionException when a Triangle comes in.
